`src/core/dispatcher.ts` derives the ordinary next-node `headSha` only from completed `prepare-pr` or `verify` records; when `verify-1` is selected immediately after `implement-1`, neither exists, so the implementation head is omitted.

The remediation path in `src/core/dispatcher.ts` supplies new round nodes with the latest `prepare-pr` head, which can bind `verify-2` to the prior round rather than the newly completed `implement-2` head.

`src/workflows/work-on.ts` records only `baseSha` in initial bounded-node queued, launch-intent started, and receipt-bound resumed payloads; it does not project `node.headSha` into those events or their durable snapshot.

`src/workflows/work-on.ts` forwards `reviewHeadSha` only for reviewer nodes. Although its launch input carries the node object, verify has no equivalent trusted head binding or dispatch-time clean-worktree/head assertion.

`src/adapters/subagents.ts` includes only the frozen base SHA in bounded task text. Approved check names are rendered only by the legacy unbounded work-on prompt; the bounded verify prompt receives no command-name list.

`src/adapters/subagents.ts` does place the validated policy's full `verificationCommands` map in the protected extension binding, and `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` makes `forge_verify` reject unknown names, but the read-only model has no supported way to enumerate that opaque map.
Existing tests cover frozen reviewer heads and the generic bounded investigate prompt, but do not assert implementation-head or approved-check-name handoff for bounded verify nodes.
